memory_lessons.applicability: Use the measured flattened-tile parallel candidate as the direct comparator; these prior results do not establish a benefit from row-band ownership.
memory_lessons.claim: The serial blocked 4x4 variant measured 0.283056 s mean, the packed variant 0.072814 s, and the parallel-tile variant 0.033899 s. All three were reported valid; their timings are observations, not proof of the mechanism behind each result.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare this row-band variant on all official sizes and collect repeated native n=1024 timings against the flattened-tile candidate.

proposal.hypothesis: With the 32x64x64 blocking and scalar 4x4 register microkernel held constant, parallelizing whole row bands rather than a flattened row/column tile loop may reduce tile-index arithmetic and scheduling work. At n=1024, static flattened scheduling already gives contiguous groups, so any gain may be small; limiting workers by row-band count may also reduce parallelism on smaller sizes. The candidate remains unmeasured.

retained: Replace size-specific matrix-multiply branches with a generic n path and bounds-safe edge handling.
Use 32x64 output blocks and 64-element reduction blocks with a scalar 4x4 output microkernel.

Assign each 32-row band, including all its column blocks, to one static OpenMP loop iteration; cap workers by both the caller thread count and row-band count, with serial execution when OpenMP is unavailable or one worker is requested.
Initialize accumulators to zero on the first reduction block and store all output elements on every call, without a separate C initialization pass.
